indicator.name: S&P 500 Constituents Above 200-day Average
indicator.description: The percentage of current S&P 500 constituents trading above their own 200-day averages.
indicator.methodology: For each trading day, the percentage of the current S&P 500 constituent list whose adjusted close exceeds its own 200-trading-day simple moving average. The component is trend-oriented: higher breadth maps to a higher score through a historical percentile.
indicator.limitations: Current constituents are used for the whole history, so the series has survivorship bias and is not a fully representative point-in-time history. History is limited to the configured lookback (six years by default). Adjusted closes are used for splits and distributions. This is a breadth condition, not a valuation measure.
